working_title: Self-Evolution Should Not Depend on How Skills Are Split
paper_type: principle + exact diagnostic certificate + released-system evidence
central_question: When can a self-evolving skill controller change its induced semantic control exposure solely because the same capability/support is represented by different skill package identities or groupings?
thesis: The relevant failure is not redundancy or overlap prevalence itself. For a frozen independently defined support-incidence matrix A, package-only control is representation-safe exactly when nonnegative package weights can equalize all covered semantic contexts. The tight finite-support distortion R*(A) identifies when this is impossible. Released Skill-SP tool-call support has R*=2 and replicates on a tool-disjoint heldout subset, while two real negative regimes have R*=1, including a logical-skill domain with 127/128 multi-membership. This isolates non-equalizable support geometry as the mechanism.

submission_claims.claim: Released self-evolving skill systems exhibit package-identity representation sensitivity on real control surfaces even when semantic content is unchanged.
support: Skill-SP: 348 released-validator-covered API-Bank rows, 183 multi-membership; released text duplicate filter misses all 5/5 observed specific-generic support-overlap pairs; exact-coverage pruning leaves 71 overlapping rows.
SkillRL: all 12 exact-content fresh-ID general-skill clones are admitted; 11/12 targets alter the unique fixed-budget semantic retrieval set and 5/12 reduce unique general content.
submission_claims.boundary: Control-plane representation sensitivity only; no downstream utility-harm claim.

submission_claims.claim: For finite first-party support matrix A, R*(A)=min t subject to w>=0 and 1<=Aw<=t1 is the exact package-only equalizability certificate: R*=1 iff exact equal exposure exists; R*>1 is the tight minimum multiplicative distortion.
support: Theorem 1 globally-singleton+overlap witness gives interpretable R*>=2 sufficient condition and is tight on released Skill-SP Level-1 support.
submission_claims.boundary: Frozen additive support exposure only; no dynamic/utility inference.

submission_claims.claim: The STRI residual tracks non-equalizable support geometry rather than overlap prevalence.
support: Skill-SP Level-1 full: 314 covered, 183 multi-membership, R*=2.
Outcome-blind frozen calibration tools: 47 covered, 33 multi-membership, R*=2.
Tool-disjoint heldout tools: 52 covered, 38 multi-membership, R*=2.
Skill-SP Level-3: 34 covered, zero multi-membership, R*=1.
Skill-SP logical first-party compiler domain: 128/128 author-contract-valid, 127/128 multi-membership, but R*=1 because released skill_008 is an umbrella alignment support.
submission_claims.boundary: The logical result is a real negative mechanism boundary, not evidence that overlap is harmless in general.

method_or_protocol.name: STRI-Cert
method_or_protocol.positioning: sound theorem-derived diagnostic/audit protocol, not a learned optimizer and not claimed computationally superior to linear programming
method_or_protocol.input: frozen independently defined context-by-package support incidence matrix
outputs: exact R*(A) and optimal package weights
optional globally-singleton overlap witness/lower bound for interpretability
UNRESOLVED only when support truth or optimization is unavailable
method_or_protocol.same_information_reduction: the exact optimal nonnegative package-weight LP is not a competing baseline hidden from the method; it is the core exact certificate. Closed-form witnesses are explanatory sufficient certificates layered on the exact LP.
method_or_protocol.novelty_claim: Novelty is the STRI scientific object, exact representation-dependence certificate for self-evolving skill support geometry, and released-system empirical boundary; not the use of an LP solver itself.

mechanism.name: Non-Equalizable Support Geometry
mechanism.old_rejected_mechanism: overlap/multiplicity itself causes irreducible representation dependence
mechanism.definition: A package-indexed control surface has a static STRI residual on a frozen support domain iff R*(A)>1. High overlap may still be representation-safe when an equalizing package mixture exists; conversely mandatory unique regions plus shared regions can force R*>1.
mechanism.interpretable_special_case: true globally singleton support cells for a and b plus a shared a+b cell imply R*>=2

strongest_reviewer_objection: Without downstream performance consequences, STRI could be viewed as an architectural fairness/normalization diagnostic rather than a practical self-evolution failure. The paper must therefore foreground the exact invariance principle, demonstrate that existing dedup/pruning/global weighting do not explain the positive domain, and use the high-overlap R*=1 logical negative to show the certificate isolates a nontrivial mechanism rather than merely counting overlap.
response_to_objection: Do not overclaim harm. Show that package identity is an endogenous evolution control variable in released systems, prove an exact representation-dependence criterion, validate it on independent positive/negative real support regimes, and separate the scientific invariance failure from any downstream utility hypothesis.
